title: Training a cleaner to observed competence, task by task
moduleTitle: Shared: Growing and managing a team
audience: Team leads and supervisors who train new and existing cleaners, and who need to show that each person is trained for the specific tasks they are allocated.
learningOutcomes: Describe the stages a cleaner moves through, from induction to observed competence in each task.
Keep a training record by person, task and date, and identify which tasks a person is not yet authorised to do.
Explain the difference between attending training and being assessed as competent in a task.

instruction.heading: Training is a sequence, not a single course
instruction.body: A cleaner moves through several stages. Induction covers the site rules, hazards, equipment and the route for reporting problems. Mandatory training covers workplace safety and infection-prevention content the site requires. Supervised practice on live work puts the new cleaner beside a trained person who watches, corrects and signs off each task. Where the role calls for it, supervisory and leadership development follows. Each stage builds on the one before, and a later stage does not make up for a gap in an earlier one.

instruction.heading: Attendance is not the same as competence
instruction.body: Attending a session shows the person received information. Competence is the demonstrated ability to carry out a task to the standard, and a supervisor records it by observation. The UK source refers to certificated competence through a UK qualification. This lesson therefore uses observation-based competence records, which work in any setting.

instruction.heading: Matching each person to the tasks they are authorised for
instruction.body: Each person's record should list the tasks they are authorised to do. A cleaner who is competent in dusting and damp mopping is not automatically authorised for machine scrubbing, chemical mixing or a specialist job. The supervisor keeps the list current, shows it on the roster or the job sheet, and removes a task from the list when training lapses or the method changes.

instruction.heading: Keeping the record current
instruction.body: Record the date, the trainer, the task, the method used, the outcome and the next review. Refresh the training when a method, product or piece of equipment changes, and after an incident or a repeated defect that suggests a gap. A record that has not been reviewed is a record that cannot show current competence.

procedure: Complete induction before a new cleaner works without direct supervision. Cover the site rules, the hazards, the equipment and the reporting route.
Schedule the mandatory training the site requires, and record attendance by name and date.
Pair the new cleaner with a trained person for supervised practice on live work. The supervisor watches, corrects and signs off each task as it is observed.
Assess each task by observation against the procedure's quality standard. Record the result as competent, not yet competent, or needs more practice.
Set the person's authorised-task list and show it on the roster or job sheet.
Repeat the training for a task when the method, product or equipment changes, or when a defect or incident suggests a gap.
Review each record at set intervals, and before any person is put forward for a supervisory role.

workedExamples.situation: A new cleaner has completed induction and a product safety session, but has not yet been observed on a damp mop. The roster now asks them to strip and seal a hard floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Are they authorised for the stripping and sealing?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Induction and a product session are not observed competence in a machine or chemical task. Keep the cleaner on tasks they are signed off for, and schedule supervised practice before any stripping or sealing work is allocated.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor's record shows a cleaner was trained in dusting two years ago, but the site has since moved to a different product and a microfibre system.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the earlier training still valid?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not for the changed method. A change in product or equipment is a trigger for retraining. Observe the cleaner using the new method, record the result, and update the authorised-task list before the method is used on the roster.

equipmentAndPpe: Current procedure for each authorised task
Observation checklist for each supervised task
Equipment and products used in training, handled as the product label directs

commonErrors.error: Recording attendance at a session as competence in a task.
commonErrors.prevention: Record competence only after the task has been observed and judged against the task standard.

commonErrors.error: Allocating a cleaner to a task that is not on their authorised list.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the list at allocation, and keep it on the roster or job sheet.

commonErrors.error: Never refreshing training after a method or product change.
commonErrors.prevention: Make any change in product, equipment or procedure a trigger for retraining, and record it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The UK source names its own training stages and a UK qualification. The qualification is not an Australian one and is not used in this lesson.

Completing this lesson or any training session does not give a licence, a certificate or authority to perform regulated work. Where a task needs a licence or authorisation, that requirement applies separately.
The WHS duty to inform, train and supervise workers is set out in the general duties lesson (shared/team/“WHS duties and consultation”).

qualityStandard: Every cleaner has a completed induction record before working without direct supervision.
Each authorised task has an observed competence entry.
The authorised-task list matches the roster and is reviewed at set intervals.
Retraining is recorded after each method, product or equipment change.
documentationEvidence: Retraining log with the trigger noted
summary: Training runs from induction through to observed competence in each task.
The authorised-task list controls allocation, and a method change triggers retraining.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which record shows that a cleaner can carry out a task safely?
options: A certificate showing attendance at a general session.
An observed competence entry for that task, made by a supervisor.
The induction sign-off from the first day and the first week

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner completed induction last month but has not been observed on machine work. What should the supervisor do?
options: Allocate machine work, because induction covered it and the cleaner is keen
Keep the cleaner off machine work until supervised practice is signed off.
Let the cleaner learn on the job from the first shift with a colleague nearby

knowledgeChecks.question: When does an existing cleaner need retraining?
options: Only at induction, and again after each new contract and never after that for the cleaner
When a product, piece of equipment or procedure changes, or when a defect suggests a gap.
Only when the cleaner asks for it and only after a formal complaint is made by the client

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say a training record must include?
options: The date, the trainer, the task, the method used, the outcome and the next review
